title: Democrats Reclaim Senate, Eye Full Control of Congress in Midterm Surge
snippet: A historic wave of Democratic flips in key battleground states, including Texas and the American South, puts the party on the brink of unified control on Capitol Hill.
content:
WASHINGTON — In a major realignment of power on Capitol Hill, Democrats have officially regained control of the U.S. Senate and appear well-positioned to retake the House of Representatives, handing Republicans and President Donald Trump a significant setback in Tuesday's midterm elections.

Crucial Flips Reshape the Senate

The party's path back to the majority was paved by notable victories in traditionally conservative and battleground terrain. In Texas, Democrat James Talarico made history by defeating Republican Ken Paxton, securing the Lone Star State's first Democratic U.S. Senate victory since 1988.

Democrats also notched vital pickups across the South and Midwest. In North Carolina, former Governor Roy Cooper unseated Republican Michael Whatley, while Annie Andrews flipped a seat in South Carolina by defeating GOP incumbent Sen. Darline Graham. In Ohio, former Sen. Sherrod Brown reclaimed his seat by defeating incumbent Republican Sen. Jon Husted. Meanwhile, in Georgia, incumbent Democratic Sen. Jon Ossoff successfully defended his seat against Republican challenger Rep. Mike Collins.

Flipping the Script in Congress

Heading into Election Night, Republicans held a 53–45 advantage in the Senate, alongside two independents who caucus with Democrats. To reclaim the majority leader's gavel, Democrats needed a net gain of four seats—a benchmark the Associated Press confirmed they achieved before midnight, with several additional uncalled races still tipping in their favor.

A similar shift appears underway in the House of Representatives. Starting the night with a narrow 218–214 majority, Republicans needed to hold their ground, but early returns indicate Democrats are on pace to far exceed the net gain of three seats required to take back the gavel.

Historic Milestones in Gubernatorial Races

Statewide executive races also produced unprecedented historic milestones across the country. In Georgia, Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms became the first Black woman elected governor in U.S. history. Ohio voters elected Democrat Amy Acton as the state's first female governor, while in Florida, Republican Byron Donalds won his race to become the state's first Black governor-elect.

Trump Distances Himself from Results

The night's outcomes follow an aggressive late-campaign push by President Trump, whose approval ratings remain near historic lows. In the weeks leading up to Election Day, Trump held rallies across swing states, urging his supporters to vote as if he were personally on the ticket.

However, as the scale of the GOP's losses became clear, Trump took to Truth Social late Tuesday to push back against suggestions that the evening served as a referendum on his leadership.

"I wasn’t on the Ballot and if I was, we would have won IN A LANDSLIDE!" Trump wrote. "Thank you for your attention to this matter."
